# Network profiles

A network profile restricts the network destinations a VM can reach. All destinations are denied unless allowed. brig enforces profiles outside the VM, so nothing in the VM can lift them.

A VM has one profile, [fence 2](glossary.md#fence-2). `brig create --profile` and `brig update --profile` pick it, and [`defaults.network_profile`](config.md#defaults.network_profile) in `config.yaml` picks the one for VMs that do not say. A change applies when the VM next starts.

## Built-in profiles

| Profile | Allows | `internet` | `host` | `host_ports` | `lan` | `ipv6` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | internet | `true` | `false` | `[]` | `false` | `false` |
| `isolated` | nothing outside the VM | `false` | `false` | `[]` | `false` | `false` |
| `open` | internet, LAN, all host services, IPv6 | `true` | `true` | `[]` | `true` | `true` |

A profile in `config.yaml` with the name of a built-in one replaces it as a whole.

## Keys of a profile

### internet

Type: boolean. Default: `false`.

Allows destinations outside the host, LAN and special-purpose address ranges.

### host

Type: boolean. Default: `false`.

Allows all services on the host's loopback interface. Without it, the host's own addresses are blocked too.

### host_ports

Type: list of port numbers. Default: `[]`.

Allows these TCP ports (1 to 65535) on the host's loopback interface even when host is false, e.g. a local model server.

### lan

Type: boolean. Default: `false`.

Allows private, shared, link-local and multicast address ranges, and the networks of the host's own addresses and routes other than default ones, such as a VPN's intranet, when the VM starts.

### ipv6

Type: boolean. Default: `false`.

Allows IPv6 traffic; otherwise the VM gets no IPv6 connectivity.

## Your own profile

Add it to `network_profiles` in `config.yaml`. This one allows the internet and a model server on the host:

```yaml
network_profiles:
  ollama:
    internet: true
    host_ports: [11434]
```
